title: The colour of the light — Image Wiki

rules.rule: If a surface is neutral (e.g., white paper), its observed colour indicates the light's colour; if it changes hue, the light has changed.
rules.evidence: The neutral is the giveaway — the paper has nothing of its own to contribute, so its chroma goes from 2 to 56 and it simply becomes the colour of the bulb.

rules.rule: If a surface is coloured (e.g., scarlet), its observed hue remains relatively stable even when the light changes significantly.
rules.evidence: The scarlet barely moves; the light is already near its hue.

rules.rule: If lit and shadow sides of the same object show identical hue but different value, suspect a render or composite rather than natural lighting.
rules.evidence: If lit and shadow differ only in darkness, and every neutral in frame is perfectly grey, suspect a render with one white light — or a composite.
